summary: Read a binary tree. Find how many nodes are visited on the shortest walk from the root to a nearest leaf. That count is called the minimum depth. A leaf is a node whose left child and right child are both absent. If the root connects to a child on only one side, keep walking until a real leaf, and do not treat the root as the end. A root alone answers one, and an empty tree answers zero. Write the answer as an integer. Stored integers may include 20, and the depth is unrelated to those integers.
notes: The left column is this sample's input text and the right column is the text the program should print. Comparison ignores trailing newlines.
